name: EXP-LIFE-001 A dry-run must not write, and delivery must survive a merge
goal:
A --dry-run that writes is a lie with a commit behind it, and delivery that needs a branch name cannot
survive the merge that proves the work landed. Both were hit while closing expedition 2c9c6c62a727ece8 after
PR #344 merged as 8b8dce2692588417764630e6c2bb6aad116d6d05.

All five findings below are reproduced, with the exact commands and the state before and after.

A. `seal --dry-run` MUTATES THE LEDGER AND COMMITS.
   Command: synth expedition seal --id 2c9c6c62a727ece8 --merge-commit 8b8dce26... --dry-run
   HEAD before: 6a2cd03 (ledger repair). HEAD after: 253de748bebba0a8d19e7a02bc09c693596dc6a0,
   "chore(synth): EXPEDITION_INTEGRATED expedition 2c9c6c62". It wrote EXPEDITION_INTEGRATED to
   .synth/data/event-stream/partition-1/segment-0001.jsonl and set
   metadata.integration = {mergeCommit: 8b8dce26..., integratedAt: 457} on the expedition record.
   Its own output reported ledger.committed = true with that hash, so it did not conceal the write - but
   --dry-run must not write at all, and the operator's only signal was a flag the tool honoured in name.
   The sibling verbs get this right, measured the same way:
     * deliver --dry-run: HEAD unchanged, and it says "Dry-run: nothing pushed, no ledger event written".
     * create --dry-run: exactly one commit and one EXPEDITION_CREATED event for draft 2c13ca22fb8c4e6c,
       both attributable to the real create that followed.
   So the contract is understood inside this one verb family; seal alone violates it.

B. `deliver` CANNOT SURVIVE A MERGED PULL REQUEST.
   Command: synth expedition deliver --id 2c9c6c62a727ece8 --no-push
   Result: DELIVERY_TIP_UNRESOLVED, "Could not resolve the tip commit of arena/841cc45d-synth."
   Delivery keys on a branch NAME. GitHub auto-deletes head branches on merge here (arena/a3a7925a-synth
   after #343, arena/841cc45d-synth after #344), and the post-merge clone is shallow with the merge commit
   grafted and no parents, so the pre-merge tip 64ea89c and every ancestor are ABSENT locally and cannot be
   recovered without network access to a branch that no longer exists.
   This is not a one-off: it is the root cause of the standing backlog. 30 expeditions sit delivery-pending
   and 24 of them are derivable from main by ID alone, yet none can be delivered through this path.

C. DRY-RUN FIDELITY: a dry-run that cannot fail the way the real verb fails is false assurance.
   deliver --dry-run returned status ok, branch arena/841cc45d-synth, branchSource executionBranch,
   wouldPush false - and never performed the tip resolution the real verb requires, so it could not predict
   the DELIVERY_TIP_UNRESOLVED that followed seconds later.

D. SEAL ASSERTS WHAT IT CANNOT VERIFY.
   With no delivery record in existence, seal accepted the merge commit and reported
   detail = "Merge commit 8b8dce26 contains the delivered tip". No tip was ever delivered, and containment
   is unverifiable in this clone because the merge commit is grafted with no parents. Under the
   four-valued rule this framework already uses elsewhere - corroborated | contradicted | unverified |
   unavailable - that is "unavailable", stated as fact.

E. A TERMINAL EXPEDITION CANNOT BE ANNOTATED.
   synth expedition refine --id 2c9c6c62a727ece8 --note <correction> returned LifecycleBlocked:
   "Expedition 2c9c6c62a727ece8 is completed; cannot refine a terminal expedition. Only draft, approved,
   committed, executing, or paused expeditions can be refined."
   So a mistake or discovery made AFTER an expedition closes cannot be recorded against it. This draft
   exists because the correction had nowhere else to go.

RESULTING STATE, STATED PLAINLY
2c9c6c62a727ece8 is now SEALED WITHOUT A DELIVERY RECORD. This was deliberately not undone: the ledger is
append-only and hand-editing event-stream or canonical-state is forbidden, so this goal text is the
correction instead of a rewrite. The integration itself is TRUE and independently verified - main contains
locateEventLog in src/cli/synth.ts (4 sites) and tests/verify-engine.test.js (14 sites),
proof/expeditions/2c9c6c62a727ece8/ is in main, and `git diff main -- src tests` is empty. What is missing is
only the delivery record (branch + tip), which cannot now be produced honestly.

STANDING CONSTRAINTS THESE VIOLATE (operator's own framing, still governing)
  * A dry-run must not write.
  * seal means "someone with authority accepted it" - it is an assertion about authority, not a VCS lookup.
  * An adapter may enrich a lifecycle transition, never authorize it.
  * Any parameter the no-VCS world does not need is a parameter the ledger must not require.
  * Steady state must require NOTHING after a merge.
  * Branch names are not durable handles - head branches are auto-deleted and the ruleset allows merge,
    squash and rebase, all of which rewrite or remove them. Commits and main's history are durable.

DELIVERABLES
  1. `seal --dry-run` writes nothing, and a guard test proves dry-run purity across the WHOLE expedition verb
     family (create, commit, start, refine, complete, deliver, seal, abandon, archive) by asserting HEAD,
     event count and record bytes are unchanged - so this cannot regress one verb at a time again.
  2. Every dry-run performs the same validation as its real verb and returns the same failure codes.
     deliver --dry-run must report DELIVERY_TIP_UNRESOLVED exactly when the real one would.
  3. `deliver` accepts a commit-ish (merge commit or tip sha) and records a COMMIT; branch becomes optional
     metadata. Delivery of a merged PR must succeed with only main's history present - shallow-safe, no
     network, no dependence on a branch that GitHub already deleted.
  4. `seal` refuses, or explicitly flags, when no delivery record exists; and every containment claim carries
     a truth value plus the reason ("grafted merge commit; parents unavailable in a shallow clone").
  5. An append-only correction note that works on terminal expeditions, so post-hoc discoveries are
     recordable against the record they concern.
  6. With 3 and 4 in place, close the backlog: the 24 derivable delivery-pending expeditions; the 6 that are
     not derivable get archived with a reason rather than left pending forever.

NON-GOALS
  * No reconcile verb - derive on read; a reconcile step reproduces the backlog failure mode.
  * Do not rewrite or delete the EXPEDITION_INTEGRATED event already written. It stays, and this record
    explains it.
  * Do not change what seal MEANS, and do not make seal depend on a forge or a network call.
  * Do not add parameters the no-VCS world does not need.
  * Not the CLI monolith (EXP-CLI-001, 2c13ca22fb8c4e6c) and not the test inventory or ownership guard
    (EXP-TEST-005, 74c33996d5e7cf32), though deliver/seal handlers currently live in src/cli/synth.ts and
    will move under EXP-CLI-001 - sequence accordingly.

ACCEPTANCE
  * The dry-run purity guard fails if any verb in the family writes during --dry-run (proved by a deliberate
    temporary regression, then removed).
  * On a fresh shallow clone of main with no head branch and no network, a merged expedition can be delivered
    by commit-ish and sealed, with containment reported as corroborated or unverified - never asserted.
  * seal without a prior delivery is refused or explicitly flagged as unverified.
  * A terminal expedition can carry an append-only correction note.
  * The 24 derivable delivery-pending expeditions are closed; `synth verify` ok and `synth status` truthful.

metadata.refinementNote:
============================================================
ADDENDUM 2026-10-14 — FINDING I UPDATED: the operator flipped the setting
============================================================
Finding I below states that `delete_branch_on_merge` measured TRUE and that disabling it was an
available mitigation rather than a current fact. That is now stale, and is corrected here
append-only instead of edited in place — per finding J, `refinementNote` is a single replaced field,
so this addendum is concatenated to the prior text, which is preserved verbatim (also at commits
f3bf5f8e and 8472162).

  * Measured after the operator's change: `gh api repos/synth-framework/synth` returns
    `"delete_branch_on_merge": false`, default_branch main. PR #345 remains OPEN and MERGEABLE with
    its head branch arena/15e0fc51-synth intact.
  * Consequence: the deadline on delivering EXP-CLI-001 (2c13ca22fb8c4e6c) before PR #345 merges is
    REMOVED — `deliver --branch origin/arena/15e0fc51-synth` will resolve after the merge. Delivery
    is still PENDING and still an explicit operator-facing assertion; nothing is delivered by this
    note, and an adapter may enrich a lifecycle transition but never authorize one.
  * The fact now lives in-repo where an agent can find it, as finding I required: AGENTS.md gained a
    "Delivery, seal and branch durability" section (commit 2188a9a) stating the setting, how to
    verify it, that it is not retroactive, and that it is a GitHub admin toggle rather than a ledger
    guarantee.
  * Unchanged by this: finding B (deliver keys on a mutable name whose durability is controlled by an
    admin toggle the ledger cannot see — deliver-by-commit-ish remains the repair, the toggle is
    mitigation), finding G (delivery records store a ref path where resolveDeliveryBranch computes
    canonicalBranch), finding H (origin has 12 heads; the branches of the 24 derivable
    delivery-pending expeditions were deleted before the setting changed and are not recoverable by
    it), and finding J (no append-only correction channel — this addendum is the workaround again).
  * One further observation for whoever owns the lifecycle: because the toggle can be flipped back by
    anyone with admin, a delivery record written against a branch NAME can become unresolvable later
    with no action inside this repository. If deliver-by-commit-ish is built, the commit-ish should
    be primary and the name commentary — the inverse of today's record shape, which is what made
    2c9c6c62a727ece8 undeliverable in the first place.

============================================================
FINDING I — OPERATOR DECISION 2026-10-14: head-branch auto-deletion can be turned off
============================================================
The operator states they can skip auto-deletion on GitHub. Measured at the time of writing, the
repository setting is still ON: `gh api repos/synth-framework/synth` returns
`"delete_branch_on_merge": true` (allow_merge_commit / allow_squash_merge / allow_rebase_merge all
true, default_branch main). So this is an available mitigation, not a current fact — and until it is
flipped, finding B's urgency stands unchanged.

What turning it off WOULD fix:
  * `deliver --branch origin/<name>` stays resolvable after a merge, so the workaround used for
    2c9c6c62a727ece8 — operator manually restores the branch on GitHub, then an explicit-refspec
    fetch `<b>:refs/remotes/origin/<b>` because this clone's refspec is single-branch, then
    `--deepen` until the merge commit has parents — is not needed for future merges.
  * seal's containment claim stays corroborable by name as well as by commit-ish.
  * The deadline I put on delivering EXP-CLI-001 before PR #345 merges disappears, but ONLY if the
    setting is off before that merge. It is on right now.

What it does NOT fix — all of this stays open:
  * Finding B remains a design defect. `deliver` keys on a mutable name whose durability is
    controlled by a repository admin toggle that the ledger knows nothing about, and that anyone with
    admin can flip back. A delivery record's resolvability should not depend on a GitHub setting.
    Deliver-by-commit-ish is still the repair; the toggle is mitigation.
  * Finding H is unaffected and not retroactive: origin currently has 12 heads, and the branches of
    the 24 derivable delivery-pending expeditions were already deleted. Disabling auto-deletion now
    does not bring them back, so those still need deliver-by-commit-ish or derivation from
    origin/main by ID.
  * Finding G is unaffected (the delivery record stores a ref path like `origin/arena/...` although
    `resolveDeliveryBranch` computes `canonicalBranch`).
  * The setting is repo-scoped and INVISIBLE to the ledger: nothing under .synth records whether
    names are durable, so no future agent can tell from the repository whether `deliver` by name is
    safe. If the operator flips it, that fact needs to live somewhere discoverable in-repo
    (AGENTS.md or docs), not only in GitHub settings. Note this must NOT become a network call in
    `status` or `doctor` — reads stay offline.

============================================================
FINDING J — the ledger has no append-only correction channel for an expedition record
============================================================
Discovered while trying to record finding I, by checking before writing:
  * `refinementNote` is a SINGLE replaced field (src/domain/planning.ts:254 sets
    `refinementNote: note`; src/runtime/replay.ts:489 replays it the same way). A second refine
    overwrites the first. There is no notes array and no history on the record.
  * There is no `decide`, `discover`, `note` or `annotate` verb — `expedition` offers only refine,
    evidence and finish for this purpose, and `discoveries` / `decisions` arrays on the record exist
    but stay empty (0 and 0 on both 73c5c033360fecf3 and 2c13ca22fb8c4e6c) because nothing writes them.
  * Combined with finding E (a terminal expedition cannot be refined at all: "cannot refine a
    terminal expedition", LifecycleBlocked), the consequence is that an expedition record cannot
    accumulate corrections. Before completion, a correction silently replaces what it corrects;
    after completion, it cannot be written at all.
  * This is why EXP-CLI-001's over-broad completion (2c13ca22fb8c4e6c, completed at 103ee921 with
    its prose ACCEPTANCE unmet) could only be corrected by creating a NEW expedition (EXP-CLI-003,
    e47a186cb472a20a) that restates the unmet criteria, plus a note in the attached evidence and in
    PR #345's body. The record itself still says only "completed".
  * The note you are reading was therefore assembled by reproducing the previous refinement note
    VERBATIM above and appending to it, because refining without doing so would have erased findings
    F, G and H from the record. That manual concatenation is the workaround, and needing it is the
    defect. Git history preserves the prior text at commit f3bf5f8e either way.
  * Remedy to consider: make refine append (a notes array with ids and timestamps), or expose the
    already-present `discoveries` / `decisions` arrays through a verb, and allow annotation of
    terminal expeditions for corrections that do not change lifecycle state — an adapter may enrich a
    lifecycle transition but never authorize one, and appending a correction authorizes nothing.

============================================================
PRESERVED VERBATIM BELOW: the previous refinement note (findings F, G, H and the delivery recipe),
reproduced in full because `refinementNote` is replaced, not appended — see finding J.
============================================================

RESOLUTION AND THREE FURTHER FINDINGS, after the operator restored branch arena/841cc45d-synth on origin (2026-10-13). The delivery record that finding B said could not be produced honestly now exists, and the containment claim finding D called unverifiable is now CORROBORATED by independent git evidence. WHAT WORKED, exactly: (1) `git fetch origin arena/841cc45d-synth:refs/remotes/origin/arena/841cc45d-synth` - a plain `git fetch origin <branch>` was NOT enough, because this clone's refspec is single-branch and the fetch only populated FETCH_HEAD, leaving the name unresolvable. The explicit refspec creates a remote-tracking ref without creating a local branch or moving HEAD. (2) `expedition deliver --id 2c9c6c62a727ece8 --branch origin/arena/841cc45d-synth --no-push` succeeded: EXPEDITION_DELIVERED, commit c7651ce342bb1fc240d00bcd50d23e6d2c3b76c2, tipCommit 64ea89c3626992fc49323aea3b17784686d60023, deliveryPending false. resolveDeliveryBranch's documented origin/ path is the right mechanism and worked as written. (3) Containment was STILL unverifiable at that point: `git merge-base --is-ancestor <tip> <merge>` exited 1 because merge commit 8b8dce26 was grafted with an empty parent list in this shallow clone - the tip object being present is not sufficient. (4) `git fetch --deepen 30 origin` exposed the parents: 8b8dce26 now reports parents [bb8809ae 64ea89c3], and `git merge-base --is-ancestor 64ea89c3... 8b8dce26...` exits 0. CORROBORATED. So deliverable 4 has a concrete recipe to encode: resolve the tip, then test ancestry; if the merge commit is grafted, report 'unavailable (shallow clone; parents not fetched)' with the deepen command as the next step, and only report 'corroborated' when is-ancestor actually exits 0. Never assert containment from the presence of a tip alone. FINDING F - lifecycle order is not enforced in either direction. deliver succeeded on an expedition that was already sealed/integrated. The record now timestamps the inversion: metadata.integration.integratedAt = 457 precedes metadata.delivery.deliveredAt = 462. Nothing refused, warned, or flagged it. Either order must be enforced, or the out-of-order case must be recorded as an anomaly on the face of the record. FINDING G - the delivery record names a REF PATH, not a branch. metadata.delivery.branch was stored as 'origin/arena/841cc45d-synth' (the remote-tracking form used to resolve it) while metadata.executionBranch already holds the canonical 'arena/841cc45d-synth'. resolveDeliveryBranch computes canonicalBranch for exactly this case and the ledger discards it. A delivery record should name the branch; the ref path is how it was found, not what it is. FINDING H - restoring branches is not a scalable fix for the backlog. This one closed because the operator manually recreated the branch on origin. The other 24 derivable delivery-pending expeditions had their head branches auto-deleted and cannot be restored one by one, so deliverable 3 (deliver by commit-ish, recording a COMMIT, shallow-safe and offline against main's own history) remains the only path that scales. Note also that this run re-verified deliver --dry-run as genuinely read-only (HEAD and the 462-line event count unchanged before and after), which sharpens finding A: seal is the only verb in the family that writes during --dry-run. INVARIANTS HELD throughout: no local branch was created for arena/841cc45d-synth (only refs/remotes/origin/...), HEAD stayed on the session branch arena/15e0fc51-synth, main stayed at 8b8dce26, the working tree stayed clean, and nothing was pushed to any branch.
